extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, IP practitioners and clients interested in European/UPC patent law
extracted.subtask_description: Summarises the EPO Enlarged Board of Appeal decision G1/24 on how claims must be interpreted when assessing patentability under the EPC, and the practical implications for examination and litigation. Focused on use of the description and drawings in claim interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims are the starting point and basis for assessing patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: “The claims are the starting point and the basis for assessing the patentability of an invention under Articles 52 to 57 EPC.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims form the primary reference for patentability assessment, but they do not stand alone; interpretation must proceed from the claim language as the basis for analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description and drawings shall always be consulted to interpret the claims
rubrics_metrics.description: “The description and drawings shall always be consulted to interpret the claims when assessing the patentability of an invention under Articles 52 to 57 EPC, and not only if the person skilled in the art finds a claim to be unclear or ambiguous when read in isolation.” (EBA headnote)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EBA rejects the approach that the description/figures are only relevant where a claim is ambiguous. Practitioners and examiners must therefore routinely refer to the description and figures when construing claim terms for patentability assessments. This resolves divergent Board of Appeal case law and aligns EPO practice with national courts and the UPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply Article 69(1) second sentence and Protocol on Interpretation when assessing patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Question posed: whether Article 69(1), second sentence EPC and Article 1 of the Protocol on the Interpretation of Article 69 EPC are to be applied on the interpretation of patent claims when assessing patentability under Articles 52 to 57 EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EBA extracted and endorsed interpretative principles from case law (including the headnote above), indicating that the Article 69 framework and its Protocol are relevant to claim interpretation in patentability assessments, even though the EPC articles themselves do not provide a fully explicit framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions or similar information in the description are relevant to claim interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Referral question: 'May a definition or similar information on a term used in the claims which is explicitly given in the description be disregarded when interpreting the claims to assess patentability and, if so, under what conditions?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given the EBA's conclusion that the description and drawings must always be consulted, explicit definitions in the description are prima facie relevant when construing claim terms. The article notes the question was referred, but does not set out detailed conditions under which such a definition could be disregarded; practitioners should therefore treat descriptively provided definitions as influential in claim construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners should carry out high-quality clarity examination under Article 84 EPC
rubrics_metrics.description: The EBA notes the 'importance of the examining division carrying out a high quality examination of whether a claim fulfils the clarity requirements of Article 84 EPC.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because examiners are now expected to consult the description/drawings as part of routine claim interpretation, there may be an increase in clarity objections. Applicants should anticipate greater scrutiny of claim wording and consider clearer claim drafting and consistency with the description to avoid objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow UPC jurisprudence that description/drawings are explanatory aids
rubrics_metrics.description: The EBA's approach is consistent with the UPC Court of Appeal statement that 'the description and drawings of a patent must always be used as explanatory aids for the interpretation of the patent claim and not only to resolve any ambiguities in the patent claim' (UPC_CoA_335/2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This alignment reinforces a harmonised approach across EPO and UPC practice; litigators and prosecutors should expect similar interpretative treatment in UPC proceedings and adjust drafting/litigation strategies accordingly.
